title: Ischemia-Reperfusion-Induced Acute Kidney Injury
author: Laura Ruiz Remolina
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j8gcrtw

steps.title: Place anesthetized mouse on heating pad
steps.instruction: After anesthesia, position the mouse supine on an electric blanket to maintain body temperature throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Make small midline incision
steps.instruction: Using scissors, cut a minimal incision in the linea alba at the level of the kidneys; the opening should be just large enough to work comfortably.

steps.title: Expose left renal pedicle
steps.instruction: Gently manipulate the intestinal package as little as possible, locate the renal pedicle behind the intestines (deep red) and identify the left kidney (the one on the surgeon’s right).

steps.title: Clamp pedicle and administer analgesic
steps.instruction: Clean the tissue (conjunctiva) around the pedicle with forceps, then apply artery clamps to induce ischemia; a correctly clamped kidney will darken to black within minutes. In older mice the procedure may be harder because of excess fat. After confirming ischemia, inject BUPREX analgesic at 200‑300 µL of a 1:20 dilution in saline (e.g., 15 µL BUPREX + 300 µL NaCl).

substeps.instruction: Apply artery clamps to the pedicle
Observe kidney darkening as ischemia confirmation

steps.title: Maintain ischemia for 30 minutes
steps.instruction: Keep the clamps in place for exactly 30 minutes, covering the mouse with gauze and continuously monitoring for any bleeding.

steps.title: Remove clamps to allow reperfusion
steps.instruction: Release the artery clamps; reperfusion of the kidney should be visible within a few seconds.

steps.title: Close abdomen and apply skin staples
steps.instruction: Suture the peritoneum continuously, sprinkle azole powders as needed, and close the skin using surgical staples.

steps.title: Hydrate mouse with saline injection
steps.instruction: Inject 200 µL of sterile saline intraperitoneally (or subcutaneously) to ensure the mouse is properly hydrated before recovery.
